how_to_apply: Eligible candidates can apply online for KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026 by following the steps below.
Visit the official KPSC website: kpsconline.karnataka.gov.in
If applying for the first time, complete the One Time Registration (OTR) by entering all personal details step by step and submitting them; OTR details, once submitted, cannot be edited later.
Log in to the applicant portal using your Enrollment Number/Mobile Number/Email ID and OTP.
Go to the "Apply to Post" tab, select this notification, and review the eligibility conditions/instructions displayed.
Complete the post-specific application form using the details carried over from your OTR profile.
Click "Pay Now" and complete the application fee payment via UPI, Debit Card, Credit Card, or Net Banking.
After successful payment, verify your submission status under the "Applied Post" tab and download the confirmation receipt containing a QR code.

Candidates should not close the browser or press the back/refresh button while payment is processing. If a payment shows "Processing" or "Pending," candidates must wait for the payment to complete before contacting KPSC; no manual intervention is possible during this stage. A submitted application under a particular post can only be edited by first deleting it under "Applied Post" and reapplying through the OTR profile before the last date; any fee already paid for a deleted application cannot be adjusted or refunded.
important_instructions: Candidates can apply through the official KPSC website only; applications through any other website will not be accepted. Only one application per post/category combination will be accepted; if a candidate submits more than one application for the same post, only the first valid registration will be considered and subsequent ones will be rejected. Age, educational qualification, and other eligibility conditions are determined as on the last date fixed for submission of the online application, unless otherwise specified for a particular category/relaxation. Candidates claiming reservation, age relaxation, or fee concession must upload the relevant certificates within the prescribed format and validity at the time of application; certificates not matching the notification's requirements will not be considered. Furnishing incorrect information, impersonation, using unfair means in the examination, or submitting fabricated documents will lead to disqualification/debarment from KPSC examinations and Karnataka State Civil Services employment, after giving the candidate an opportunity to be heard. KPSC does not correspond with candidates on the status of their application/candidature by phone or letter; candidates should keep checking their registered login and the KPSC website for updates. The syllabus for the Main Examination is published separately on the KPSC website: kpsc.kar.nic.in/Syllabus

content_sections.heading: KPSC Gazetted Probationers Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: As per Rule 7 of the Karnataka Recruitment of Gazetted Probationers (Appointment by Competitive Examinations) Rules, 1997 (as amended by the 8th Amendment Rules, 2010), no candidate is eligible for recruitment under these rules unless they possess a Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree awarded by a University established by law in India , or an equivalent qualification. Candidates who have appeared for an examination that would render them educationally qualified, but whose results have not yet been declared, are also eligible for admission to the Preliminary Examination; however, they must produce proof of passing the qualifying examination along with their Main Examination application, failing which they will not be admitted to the Main Examination. Candidates who have passed their final professional/medical examination but not completed internship at the time of application are provisionally admitted, subject to submitting the required proof at the time of interview. The notification does not specify a separate, distinct educational qualification for each of the 18 individual posts beyond this general Bachelor's/Master's Degree requirement under the Gazetted Probationers Rules, 1997. The age limit is prescribed as per Rule of the Gazetted Probationers Rules, 1997, along with a one-time special relaxation announced for this recruitment. As per Government Order No. ಸಕಇ 262 ಪಿಆರಇ 2025, dated 29-01-2026, candidates belonging to all categories covered under the above age-limit rules are entitled to a further one-time additional relaxation of 5 years in the maximum age limit for this recruitment. Additional age relaxation is also available as follows: Ex-servicemen get relaxation equal to their length of military service plus 3 years (subject to conditions); Persons with Disabilities get 10 years' relaxation; and candidates who are widowed/divorced and have not remarried get 10 years' relaxation, subject to the conditions specified in the notification.

content_sections.heading: KPSC Gazetted Probationers Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for the Gazetted Probationers posts under this notification follows a two-stage process as prescribed under the Gazetted Probationers Rules, 1997: a Preliminary Examination, followed by a Main Examination and Personality Test (interview) for candidates who qualify. The Preliminary Examination is objective type (multiple choice) and consists of two papers, each of 200 marks and 2 hours' duration (400 marks total). It is a screening test only; marks scored in the Preliminary Examination are not counted towards the final merit. There is negative marking of 0.25 marks (one-fourth) for every wrong answer in the Preliminary Examination. Candidates are admitted to the Main Examination in a ratio of 1:15 against notified vacancies, in order of merit, subject to category-wise representation. The Main Examination is descriptive/conventional type and consists of 5 compulsory papers, plus 2 qualifying language papers (Kannada and English). Marks in the Kannada and English qualifying papers are not counted towards merit, but candidates must score a minimum of 35% (52.5 marks) in each to qualify for the Personality Test; those who do not meet this minimum are not evaluated in the other papers. All Main Examination papers can be answered entirely in Kannada or English (except the qualifying papers) and are of degree-level standard. Candidates are called for the Personality Test in a ratio of 1:3 against notified vacancies, based on Main Examination merit, and the Personality Test carries a maximum of 25 marks. For certain posts involving field/law-and-order duties (Karnataka Police Service (Junior Scale) Group A, Karnataka Prisons Service, and Deputy Superintendent of Excise), the notification also prescribes minimum physical standards (height, chest measurement, and endurance/walking test) for male and female candidates; candidates applying for these specific posts should refer to the detailed physical standards table in the official notification.

faq.question: Q1. What is KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a recruitment drive by the Karnataka Public Service Commission to fill 319 Gazetted Probationers posts across 18 designations under Group A and Group B for the year 2026-27.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available under KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 319 vacancies are notified - 117 under Group A posts and 202 under Group B posts, including 22 posts under the Hyderabad-Karnataka local cadre.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date to apply online is 07-09-2026. Online applications began on 01-08-2026.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification required for KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must hold a Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree from a University established by law in India, or an equivalent qualification, as per the Gazetted Probationers Rules, 1997.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The minimum age is 21 years. The maximum age is 40 years for General Merit, 43 years for Category 2A/2B/3A/3B, and 45 years for SC/ST/Category-1 candidates, with a further one-time 5-year relaxation announced for this recruitment plus other category-based relaxations.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The fee is Rs. 600/- for General Merit candidates, Rs. 300/- for Category 2A/2B/3A/3B candidates, Rs. 50/- for Ex-Military Personnel, and no fee for SC/ST/Category-1/PWD candidates.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates can apply online through kpsconline.karnataka.gov.in by completing One Time Registration (OTR), selecting "Apply to Post," filling the application, paying the fee, and submitting before the last date.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for KPSC Gazetted Probationers Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Selection involves a Preliminary Examination (400 marks, screening only), a Main Examination (1250 marks across 5 papers plus 2 qualifying language papers), and a Personality Test/interview (25 marks), for a combined total of 1275 marks.

faq.answer: The notification does not specify individual pay scales for each of the 18 posts; salary and pay scale details are governed by the respective service rules of each post and are not detailed in this notification.
